translationRepairs: His father, surnamed Zhi, served in office and later relocated to Jiangdu in Yang Prefecture.
His father held office and later relocated to Jiangdu in Yang Prefecture.
父直官 means the father was serving in office; 直 is not a surname (the father was surnamed Sun), so "surnamed Zhi" is an invention.
He was summoned from the post of Fujian transport vice-commissioner to become Clerk of Works in the Ministry of Revenue.
He was summoned from the post of Fujian transport vice-commissioner to become vice director of the Bureau of State Farms.
屯田員外(郎) is the vice director of the Bureau of State Farms (Ministry of Works), not a "Clerk of Works in the Ministry of Revenue".
Soon afterward he was appointed assistant director of the Palace Domestic Service and bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.
Soon afterward he was appointed vice director of the Court of the Palace Treasury and bureau director in the Ministry of Revenue.
少府少監 is the vice director of the Palace Treasury (Shaofu); "Palace Domestic Service" renders 殿中 (s0025), a different office.
In recognition of his work in founding and planning, he was promoted to Grandee of the Palace and transferred to Yan Prefecture.
In recognition of his work in founding and planning, he was promoted to Grandee of the Palace and transferred to Yun Prefecture.
He was posthumously granted the title Silver-Green Glory Grandee of Glory, with the posthumous name "Tongjing" (Comprehensive Tranquility).
He was posthumously granted the title Grandee of Silver-Green Glory, with the posthumous name "Tongjing" (Comprehensive Tranquility).
銀青光祿大夫 is one title; "Glory Grandee of Glory" duplicates 光 and garbles it.

Zhang Shu wanted to recommend him as censor, but he firmly declined. When Emperor Huizong solicited opinions, memorials from distant officials were often rejected because their seals did not meet format requirements; Shi's submission alone got through.

Zhang Jie wanted to recommend him as censor, but he firmly declined. When Emperor Huizong solicited opinions, memorials from distant officials were often rejected because their seals did not meet format requirements; Shi's submission alone got through.
章楶 is read Zhang Jie (楶 jié), not "Zhang Shu".
Li Zhaoqi, courtesy name Chenji, was from Jinan.
Li Zhaoqi, courtesy name Chengji, was from Jinan.
成季 is romanized Chengji, not "Chenji".

He was appointed director of the Secretariat and investigating censor in Kaifeng, then soon made judicial intendant for the Yongxing, Jingxi, and Jingdong circuits; he was stripped of office for Yuanfu faction association.

He was appointed assistant director of the Palace Library and judge of Kaifeng, then soon made judicial intendant for the Yongxing, Jingxi, and Jingdong circuits; he was stripped of office for Yuanfu faction association.
秘書丞 is an assistant director of the Palace Library (not the Secretariat), and 開封推官 is a judicial judge of Kaifeng prefecture, not an investigating censor.
Han Zhongyan wanted to appoint him attendant gentleman of the household, but Zeng Bu blocked the appointment until Bu departed for the imperial tomb rites, when the order finally went out.
Han Zhongyan wanted to appoint him imperial diarist, but Zeng Bu blocked the appointment until Bu was sent out as commissioner for the imperial mausoleum, when the order finally went out.
起居舍人 is the imperial diarist of the Secretariat, not an "attendant gentleman of the household"; 布使山陵 means Zeng Bu was dispatched as mausoleum commissioner.
At the start of the Jingkang era he was again summoned as attendant gentleman of the household, but he had already died.
At the start of the Jingkang era he was again summoned as imperial diarist, but he had already died.
起居舍人 is the imperial diarist, not an "attendant gentleman of the household".
Early in the Huizong reign he served as investigating censor in the Kaifeng metropolitan office.
Early in the Huizong reign he served as judge of Kaifeng prefecture.
開封府推官 is a judicial judge of Kaifeng prefecture, not an investigating censor.
He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and with the provisional title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Xianmo Pavilion governed Yingzhou.
He was promoted to Vice Minister of Rites, then transferred to the Ministry of Revenue, and as edict attendant of the Xianmo Pavilion governed Yingzhou.
顯謨閣待制 is an Edict Attendant of the Xianmo Pavilion, not a "Gentleman for Court Discussion".

Summoned and appointed Vice Minister of War, he again received the straight title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Xianmo Pavilion to govern Chengdu but did not go; after successive transfers through five prefectures he entered court as Vice Minister of Works.

Summoned and appointed Vice Minister of War, he again was named auxiliary academician of the Xianmo Pavilion to govern Chengdu but did not go; after successive transfers through five prefectures he entered court as Vice Minister of Works.
顯謨閣直學士 is an Auxiliary Academician of the Xianmo Pavilion; "straight title of Gentleman for Court Discussion" garbles it.
As acting prefect of Weizhou he entered service to compile the Record of Trust between Lu and Wei of the Two Reigns.
After serving as vice-prefect of Weizhou he was brought to court to compile the Record of Trust between Lu and Wei of the Two Reigns.
通判 is vice-prefect, not acting prefect, and 入 means he entered the capital (court) to compile the work.

He was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then Vice Director in the Left Office and Drafting Gentleman for Court Audience, and was promoted to Drafting Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.
He was appointed Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel, then Vice Director in the Left Office and imperial diarist, and was promoted to Drafting Gentleman of the Central Secretariat.
起居舍人 is the imperial diarist, not a "Drafting Gentleman for Court Audience".

At the beginning of the Chongning era he was promoted to Chief Supervising Censor and Vice Minister of Personnel, and with the provisional title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Baowen Pavilion governed Guangzhou.
At the beginning of the Chongning era he was promoted to Chief Supervising Censor and Vice Minister of Personnel, and as edict attendant of the Baowen Pavilion governed Guangzhou.
寶文閣待制 is an Edict Attendant of the Baowen Pavilion, not a "Gentleman for Court Discussion".
Critics argued that at the end of Yuanyou Huanzhi had associated with Chen Guan, Gong Shen, and Zhang Tingjian; cast aside in the Shaosheng era, yet now restored—harmful to the inaugural policies.
Critics argued that at the end of Yuanyou Huanzhi had associated with Chen Guan, Gong Kuai, and Zhang Tingjian; cast aside in the Shaosheng era, yet now restored—harmful to the inaugural policies.
龔𡙇 is a graphic variant of 龔夬, the censor Gong Kuai who is regularly named with Chen Guan and Zhang Tingjian; "Gong Shen" is a misreading.
Eight years later he governed Zhongshan prefecture, with addition of the straight title of Gentleman for Court Discussion of the Baowen Pavilion.
Eight years later he governed Zhongshan prefecture, with addition of the title of auxiliary academician of the Baowen Pavilion.
寶文閣直學士 is an Auxiliary Academician of the Baowen Pavilion.
The Emperor immediately ordered Lian to survey and provide relief on the eastern circuits, and appointed him Assistant Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
The Emperor immediately ordered Lian to survey and provide relief on the eastern circuits, and appointed him Assistant of the Court of Agriculture.
司農丞 is an assistant of the Court of Agriculture (Sinong), not of the Ministry of Revenue.
On his return his report accorded with the Emperor's intent; he was promoted to transport assistant of Lizhou circuit, and again served as assistant director in the Ministry of Revenue.
On his return his report accorded with the Emperor's intent; he was promoted to transport assistant of Lizhou circuit, and again served as assistant of the Court of Agriculture.
丞司農 means assistant of the Court of Agriculture (Sinong), not of the Ministry of Revenue.
He was given the additional office of Collator in the Court for Collection of Precious Objects and made judicial intendant of Hedong.
He was given the additional office of Collator of the Academy of Assembled Worthies and made judicial intendant of Hedong.
集質校理 is evidently 集賢校理 (Collator of the Academy of Assembled Worthies); no "Court for Collection of Precious Objects" existed.

The following year he was promoted to Left Division Director, then transferred to Diarist, Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Writings, and Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner's Court.

The following year he was promoted to Left Division Director, then transferred to Diarist, Compiler at the Hall for Collecting Writings, and Chief Recipient of Edicts at the Bureau of Military Affairs.
樞密都承旨 is the Chief Recipient of Edicts of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
He was appointed Supervising Censor-in-Chief, then died at the age of fifty-nine.
He was appointed Supervising Secretary, then died at the age of fifty-nine.
給事中 is the Supervising Secretary of the Chancellery, not a censor-in-chief.

He was promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat, served on embassy to Liao, was given direct access to the Secret Archive, and became Shaanxi transport commissioner, governing in turn Shaan, Tan, and Qing.

He was promoted to Vice Director of the Palace Library, served on embassy to Liao, was made Auxiliary of the Secret Archive, and became Shaanxi transport commissioner, governing in turn Shaan, Tan, and Qing.
秘書少監 is the vice director of the Palace Library, and 直秘閣 is the honorary title Auxiliary of the Secret Archive, not "direct access" to it.

On his embassy to Liao he observed the great-grandson Xi to be fond of music, beautiful women, fine tea, and antique paintings. He concluded that one day there would surely appear another Zhang Yichao of Tang, who would lead the thirteen circuits back in submission—and that within forty years one would see it.

On his embassy to Liao he observed the imperial grandson Xi to be fond of music, beautiful women, fine tea, and antique paintings. He concluded that one day there would surely appear another Zhang Yichao of Tang, who would lead the thirteen prefectures back in submission—and that within forty years one would see it.
太孫 is the imperial grandson (heir-grandson) of the Liao emperor, not a great-grandson; 十三州 are prefectures, not circuits.
During the Shaoxing era he was posthumously granted the title Academic Gentlemen of the Hall for Treasuring Culture.
During the Shaoxing era he was posthumously granted the title Auxiliary Academician of the Baowen Pavilion.
寶文閣直學士 is Auxiliary Academician of the Baowen Pavilion; "Academic Gentlemen" is ungrammatical and inaccurate.
He laid out the ill of redundant offices, saying that candidates advanced by grace and favor ought to follow the Jiaoyou and Zhiping system;
He laid out the ill of redundant offices, saying that candidates advanced by grace and favor ought to follow the Jiayou and Zhiping system;
嘉祐 is the Jiayou reign period, misspelled "Jiaoyou".

The historians comment: When the Wang clan, Zhang Dun, and Cai Que held the state, scholar-officials knew that to oppose them was to be expelled and to join them was to advance. Yet Sun Gao spoke plainly against Cai Jing and would not lend him aid;

The historians comment: When Wang Anshi, Zhang Dun, and Cai Que held the state, scholar-officials knew that to oppose them was to be expelled and to join them was to advance. Yet Sun Gao spoke plainly against Cai Jing and would not lend him aid;
王氏 here is Wang Anshi (the commentary later says Sheng Tao "would not yield to Anshi"), not a clan.
He served as vice prefect of Huzhou, received direct appointment at the Hall for Collecting Writings, was transferred to Salt and Iron Commissioner, and jointly edited the Veritable Records.
He served as vice prefect of Huzhou, became Auxiliary of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, was transferred to Salt and Iron Commissioner, and served as co-compiler of the Court Diary.
直集賢院 is the title Auxiliary of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, and 同修起居注 is co-compiler of the Diary of Activity and Repose, not the Veritable Records (實錄).
Sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou, he memorialized to abolish the Yuanyuan monitor and rushed four thousand two hundred qing of pasture land into the people's hands.
Sent out as prefect of Zhengzhou, he memorialized to abolish the Yuanwu Pasturage Directorate and release four thousand two hundred qing of pasture land to the people.
原武監 is the Yuanwu (horse-pasturage) Directorate, not "Yuanyuan"; 馳 here means to relax/release, not "rush".

During the Yuanyou era he governed in turn Xiuzhou, Xiangzhou, Heyang, Cao, and Suzhou, was made Academic Gentlemen of the Collecting Writings Hall, and again served as academician-administrator at Yang, Lu, Xuan, and Ying; he died at the age of seventy-five.

During the Yuanyou era he governed in turn Xiuzhou, Xiangzhou, Heyang, Cao, and Suzhou, was made Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies, and again served as edict attendant at Yang, Lu, Xuan, and Ying; he died at the age of seventy-five.
集賢院學士 is Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies ("Academic Gentlemen" is ungrammatical), and 待制 is an edict attendant title.
Wang Yansou and others said Fu's learning and conduct were exceptional and that added posthumous honors were fitting; an edict granted five hundred thousand cash.
Wang Yansou and others said Fu's learning and conduct were exceptional and that he deserved generous funeral gifts; an edict granted five hundred thousand cash.
優賻 means generous funeral contributions (the edict then grants cash), not posthumous honors.
His son Qi, during the Jianyan era, served as Vice Censor-in-Chief under the Gate.
His son Qi, during the Jianyan era, served as Vice Director of the Chancellery.
門下侍郎 is the Vice Director of the Chancellery (Menxia), not a censorial post.
Dong Dunyi and Huang Tingji collected Sheng's faults, and he was reassigned as Academic Gentlemen of the Collecting Writings Hall.
Dong Dunyi and Huang Tingji collected Sheng's faults, and he was reassigned as Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies.
集賢院學士 is Academician of the Academy of Assembled Worthies; "Academic Gentlemen" is ungrammatical and inaccurate.

He returned as Attending Censor and Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs Commissioner's Court, advanced to Drafting Official and Vice Minister of Personnel and of Rites, and as academician-administrator of the Dragon Diagram Hall again governed Ying; he was later transferred to Guozhou.

He returned as Attending Censor and Chief Recipient of Edicts at the Bureau of Military Affairs, advanced to Drafting Official and Vice Minister of Personnel and of Rites, and as academician-administrator of the Dragon Diagram Hall again governed Ying; he was later transferred to Guozhou.
樞密都承旨 is the Chief Recipient of Edicts of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
Gong Dingchen, courtesy name Fuzhi, was from Xucheng in Yan.
Gong Dingchen, courtesy name Fuzhi, was from Xucheng in Yun.
He was transferred to judicial aide of Mengzhou and, on recommendation, became secretary to the Taizhou military governor.
He was transferred to judicial aide of Mengzhou and, on recommendation, became secretary to the Taining Army military governor.
泰寧軍 is the Taining Army (seated at Yanzhou), not Taizhou.
When Shi Jie of Cui Lai died, slanderers said Jie had fled north to Liao. An edict ordered Yanzhou to investigate.
When Shi Jie of Culai died, slanderers said Jie had fled north to Liao. An edict ordered Yanzhou to investigate.
徂徠 is Culai (Mount Culai, Shi Jie's sobriquet place), a single name, not "Cui Lai".
He was recommended as Assistant in the Secretariat and became magistrate of Laowu.
He was recommended as Assistant Editorial Director of the Palace Library and became magistrate of Laiwu.
秘書省著作佐郎 is an Assistant Editorial Director of the Palace Library (not the Secretariat), and 萊蕪 is Laiwu.

He was summoned to compile books in the History Office, transferred to a directorship in the Ministry of Revenue, and elevated to Diarist-of-the-Left with concurrent appointment as vice director of the Remonstrance Bureau.

He was summoned to compile books in the History Office, transferred to the Bureau of Criminal Administration, and elevated to Diarist-of-the-Left with concurrent appointment as vice director of the Remonstrance Bureau.
都官 is the Bureau of Criminal Administration (under the Ministry of Justice), not a Ministry of Revenue post.
Before long he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently Vice Censor-in-Chief, with third-rank court dress.
Before long he was made Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and concurrently Attending Censor in charge of Miscellaneous Affairs, with third-rank court dress.
侍御史知雜事 is the Attending Censor in charge of Miscellaneous Affairs, not the Vice Censor-in-Chief (御史中丞).
He memorialized urging the Empress Dowager to restore the regency to the emperor without delay;
He memorialized urging the Empress Dowager to return the government to the emperor without delay;
還政 means returning governing power to the emperor; "restore the regency" inverts the sense.
He held that Zhaoling should be buried frugally and the Spirit Hall at Jingling should not be enlarged, thereby displaying the late emperor's modest virtue.
He held that Zhaoling should be buried frugally and the imperial portrait hall at the Jingling Palace should not be enlarged, thereby displaying the late emperor's modest virtue.
景靈神御殿 is the imperial portrait hall within the Jingling Palace (景靈宮), not a place called Jingling.
He was made Compiler in the Hall for Cherishing Literature and prefect of Yingtian, then transferred to Jiangning.
He was made Compiler of the Academy of Assembled Worthies and prefect of Yingtian, then transferred to Jiangning.
集賢殿修撰 is Compiler of the Academy (Hall) of Assembled Worthies, not "Cherishing Literature".
He again judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and stayed at Nanjing as regent.
He again judged the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and served as Resident Governor of the Southern Capital (Nanjing).
留守南京 means serving as resident governor (liushou) of the Southern Capital, not acting as regent.
When a post in the princely household fell vacant, Remonstrance Officer Chen Xiang asked that someone be chosen; Shenzong said, "One of Zheng Mu's character is fit to attend a prince."
When a post in the princely household fell vacant, Censor Chen Xiang asked that someone be chosen; Shenzong said, "One of Zheng Mu's character is fit to attend a prince."
御史 is a censor, not a remonstrance officer.
Before his term ended he petitioned to retire and was put in charge of the Cave of the Azure Sky at Hangzhou.
Before his term ended he petitioned to retire and was put in charge of the Dongxiao Palace at Hangzhou.
洞霄宮 is the Dongxiao Daoist palace (a sinecure temple post), not a cave.
in the fifth year he was made Awaiting-Appointment Drafter of the Pavilion of Treasured Literature while still serving as Director.
in the fifth year he was made Edict Attendant of the Baowen Pavilion while still serving as Director.
寶文閣待制 is Edict Attendant of the Baowen Pavilion.
In the sixth year he asked to retire and was made intendant of the Cave of the Azure Sky.
In the sixth year he asked to retire and was made intendant of the Dongxiao Palace.
洞霄宮 is the Dongxiao Daoist palace, not a cave.
When the edict passed the Secretariat, Supervising Secretary Fan Zuyu said, "Though Mu is past seventy, his strength is still firm.
When the edict passed the Chancellery, Supervising Secretary Fan Zuyu said, "Though Mu is past seventy, his strength is still firm.
門下 is the Chancellery (Menxia), not the Secretariat.

He was appointed Remonstrating Censor, pacification commissioner of Jingdong East Circuit, and concurrently prefect of Qingzhou; he was promoted to Grandee of the Palace, requested retirement on grounds of age, and was made intendant of the Taiping Palace in Bozhou.

He was appointed Grand Master of Remonstrance, pacification commissioner of Jingdong East Circuit, and concurrently prefect of Qingzhou; he was promoted to Grandee of the Palace, requested retirement on grounds of age, and was made intendant of the Taiqing Palace in Bozhou.
諫議大夫 is Grand Master of Remonstrance, and 太清宮 is the Taiqing Palace, not Taiping.
Shortly afterward he retired with the rank of Grandee of Direct Remonstrance; he was seventy-seven, and died in the first year of Yuanyou.
Shortly afterward he retired with the rank of Grandee of Proper Counsel; he was seventy-seven, and died in the first year of Yuanyou.
正議大夫 is the prestige title Grandee of Proper Counsel; it has nothing to do with remonstrance.
Huizong summoned him for audience and promoted him to Right Remonstrance Officer, then to Right Imperial Censor.
Huizong summoned him for audience and promoted him to Right Exhorter, then to Right Remonstrator.
右正言 is the Right Exhorter and 右司諫 the Right Remonstrator; neither is a censor.
Vice Censor-in-Chief Qian Kui led his colleagues in asking that the Yuanyou Empress be deposed and Lady Liu installed as Empress Dowager; Dan confronted him face to face that this could not be done.
Vice Censor-in-Chief Qian Yu led his colleagues in asking that the Yuanyou Empress be deposed and Lady Liu installed as Empress Dowager; Dan confronted him face to face that this could not be done.
錢遹: 遹 is read yù, so the name is Qian Yu, not "Qian Kui".
Kui impeached Dan for secretly aiding Yuanyou policies and had him demoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
Yu impeached Dan for secretly aiding Yuanyou policies and had him demoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
遹 is read yù; the given name is Yu, not "Kui".

The emperor, because his memorial contained the phrase "bewitching the late emperor," took it as a personal attack and soon transferred him to Vice Minister of Personnel and made him Awaiting-Appointment Drafter of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Xuanzhou.

The emperor, because his memorial contained the phrase "bewitching the late emperor," took it as a personal attack and soon transferred him to Vice Minister of Personnel and made him Edict Attendant of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Xuanzhou.
顯謨閣待制 is Edict Attendant of the Xianmo Pavilion.
When Hao Sui again entered attendance, Dan was made Direct Drafter of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Chengdu.
When Hao Sui again entered attendance, Dan was made Auxiliary Academician of the Xianmo Pavilion and prefect of Chengdu.
顯謨閣直學士 is Auxiliary Academician of the Xianmo Pavilion.
Soon the prefect of Weizhou, Jiao Caishu, proposed to entice Ba and Ba prefectures to submit inward.
Soon the prefect of Weizhou, Jiao Caishu, proposed to entice Bao and Ba prefectures to submit inward.
保、霸 are two different prefectures, Bao and Ba.
Gongsun soon left office under charges; Dan was promoted to Direct Drafter of the Hall for Venerating Antiquity and again made prefect of Chengdu.
Gongsun soon left office under charges; Dan was promoted to Auxiliary Academician of the Shugu Hall and again made prefect of Chengdu.
述古殿直學士 is Auxiliary Academician of the Shugu Hall.
He died at Chang'an, aged sixty-two, and was posthumously granted the title Grandee of Palace Attendance.
He died at Chang'an, aged sixty-two, and was posthumously granted the title Grandee of the Palace.
太中大夫 is the prestige title Grandee of the Palace.
His merit was entered and he was due for promotion in rank, but he declined while his parents still lived.
His merit was entered and he was due for promotion in rank, but he declined it, asking that the favor be extended to his parents instead.
辭以及父母 means he declined the promotion so that the favor would be extended to his parents, not that he declined because they were alive.
He was then transferred to transport commissioner and summoned as vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and intendant of Kaifeng's county markets.
He was then transferred to transport commissioner and summoned as assistant of the Court of Agriculture and intendant of the counties and towns of Kaifeng.
司農丞 is an assistant of the Court of Agriculture, and 提點開封縣鎮 supervises the counties and towns of Kaifeng.
He was reassigned judicial intendant for the Northwest circuit around the capital.
He was reassigned judicial intendant for the Jingxi North circuit.
京西北路 is the Jingxi North circuit.

At the opening of the Shaosheng era, Shangguan Jun dredged up charges that Zhizhong had served Lü Dafang's faction and had him appointed awaiting-appointment drafter of the Pavilion of Treasured Literature and prefect of Yan.
At the opening of the Shaosheng era, Shangguan Jun dredged up charges that Zhizhong had served Lü Dafang's faction and had him appointed edict attendant of the Baowen Pavilion and prefect of Yunzhou.
寶文閣待制 is Edict Attendant of the Baowen Pavilion, and 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not "Yan".
